provenance: Drawn from the engine's own map and Today, exported unedited from a collection built on November 5, 2026: three watches' papers from arXiv, and three searches' from the sources they asked. The papers and the day's runs are real. For the watches' earlier papers, the day each was collected, and so how bright it is drawn, is set from its publication date.

papers.title: A Laplace-Transform Green's Function for Two-Zone Diffusion with Energy Losses: Application to the Geminga Pulsar Halo
papers.authors: Furong Li, Wei Liu, Yali Shao, Yiqing Guo
papers.abstract_lede: Extended TeV gamma-ray halos around pulsars are commonly interpreted as evidence for slow diffusion of high-energy electrons and positrons near their sources, with diffusion coefficients about two orders of magnitude below the Galactic average inferred from B/C measurements.

papers.title: PathoS2VD: From 2D Histopathology to Pseudo Z-Stack Representations
papers.authors: Jiamu Wang, Keunho Byeon, Ji-Uk Kim, Jin Tae Kwak, Heounjeong Go
papers.abstract_lede: For decades, diagnostic pathology has relied on thin two-dimensional (2D) tissue sections, despite biological tissues exhibiting inherently three-dimensional (3D) morphological organization.

papers.title: Phantom: Temporal Caching for Diffusion Models
papers.authors: Yuzhe Fu, Cong Guo, Zishan Shao, Bowen Duan, Chiyue Wei, Haoxuan Shan, Ting Jiang, Hancheng Ye, Jonathan Ku, Changchun Zhou, Hai "Helen" Li, Yiran Chen
papers.abstract_lede: Diffusion models have become the dominant paradigm for high-quality image generation, but their iterative inference across tens of timesteps incurs substantial computational overhead.

papers.title: DyPSI: Dynamic Physics Sensing via Joint Field and Sensor-Trajectory Generation
papers.authors: Yizhou Zhang, Panqi Chen, Lei Cheng, Ting Zhang, Jianlong Li, Jianfeng Shi, Shikai Fang
papers.abstract_lede: Physics sensing in evolving environments requires reconstructing dense spatiotemporal fields from sparse observations while adapting where future observations should be collected.

papers.title: Spatially and Compositionally Controlled Multimodal Glioblastoma MRI Synthesis with Latent Diffusion
papers.authors: Steven Glass, Max Van Puyvelde, Marija Pizurica, Mia Meyer, Olivier Gevaert, Willie Brink
papers.abstract_lede: Glioblastoma exhibits substantial heterogeneity in tumour morphology and composition across MRI modalities, often making available clinical datasets highly unbalanced in terms of patient pathologies.

papers.title: LungMend: A Healthy-Only Latent Diffusion Shape Prior for Lung Mask Correction in Severe Tuberculosis CT
papers.authors: Rezkellah Noureddine Khiat, Pierre-Yves Brillet, Catalin Fetita
papers.abstract_lede: Lung segmentation models such as R231 are widely used, but they fail on severe tuberculosis (TB) CT: cavities and consolidations look like non-lung tissue and are left out of the mask. We present LungMend, a post-processing model that corrects such masks using only healthy anatomy.

papers.title: Dynamical State-Space Diffusion for Spatiotemporal Prediction
papers.authors: Woojun Lee, Hankyeol Kim, Pilsung Kang
papers.abstract_lede: Diffusion models for temporal prediction typically corrupt each future frame with independent noise, leaving temporal dependence entirely to the denoiser. We propose Dynamical State-Space Diffusion (DSSD), which learns the temporal structure of the corruption process itself.

papers.title: VA-TDM: A Unified View for Improving Few-Step Diffusion Models by Velocity Adversarial Distillation
papers.authors: Yihong Luo, Tianyu Pang, Tianyang Hu
papers.abstract_lede: Few-step distillation offers efficient generation with diffusion and flow models, but preserving quality with only a few sampling steps remains challenging. Distribution-matching methods via score distillation provide a strong foundation, yet they rely on accurately tracking the student's changing distribution.

papers.title: Scenario Augmentation for Rare Financial Events via Multimodal Latent Diffusion
papers.authors: Mahdi Arab Loodaricheh, Anita Raja, Indranil SenGupta
papers.abstract_lede: Extreme market movements are scarce, heterogeneous, and difficult to learn from imbalanced historical data.

papers.title: Householder Motion Embedding: Noise Modulation for Motion-Controllable Video Generation
papers.authors: Tao Jun Lin, Jinhong Ni, Ruyi Zha, Yifu Wang, Xibin Song, Pan Ji, Hongdong Li
papers.abstract_lede: Diffusion models for video generation have achieved remarkable success, yet precise motion control under explicit user guidance remains challenging. Recent noise-warping methods introduce temporal correlations by warping the noise according to the user-provided motion signal.

papers.title: MIKU: Material Invariance and Knowledge Unification for PBR Generation
papers.authors: Yajie Bao, Jiaye Fu, Youtian Lin, Shuang Wu, Jiachen Qian, Feihu Zhang, Xun Cao, Yao Yao
papers.abstract_lede: High-quality material generation for physically based rendering (PBR) remains challenging because datasets and synthesis pipelines lack standardized representations. Differences in material definitions, rendering conventions, and parameterizations lead to unstable and physically implausible results.

papers.title: OptIMerge: Optimization-Based Merging of Diffusion Models
papers.authors: Viraj Shah, Ashwini Pokle, Peyman Milanfar, Mauricio Delbracio, Hossein Talebi
papers.abstract_lede: The arithmetic merging of weights from multiple task-specific models fine-tuned from a shared base model, commonly known as model souping, has emerged as a popular strategy for multi-task learning without the computational overhead of joint retraining.

papers.title: Training-Free Predictive Spatio-Temporal Token Pruning for Few-Step Autoregressive Video Diffusion
papers.authors: Jia Li, Xurui Peng, Xing Wang, Hayden Kwok-Hay So
papers.abstract_lede: Few-step autoregressive (AR) video diffusion models generate videos chunk by chunk and have made efficient video generation practical.

papers.title: Improving Long-Tail Detection via Layout-Instruction Conditioned Diffusion Synthesis
papers.authors: Xinyu Zhang, Xiaodi Wang, Yanpeng Sun, Lingfeng Yang, Jingdong Wang, Lingqiao Liu
papers.abstract_lede: Synthetic data from diffusion models can improve object detection, but long-tail performance is still limited by scarce rare classes and inflexible conditioning (e.g., text-only or layout-only inputs).

papers.title: CoGenRec: A Unified Generative Framework for Complementary Vision Reconstruction
papers.authors: Yapeng Meng, Yuguo Chen, Xiangru Chen, Shaojun Xu, Xuezhen Wang, Lijian Wang, Zheyu Yang, Yihan Lin, Luping Shi, Rong Zhao
papers.abstract_lede: Capturing scenes with extreme motion and high dynamic range is fundamentally constrained by trade-offs among temporal resolution, spatial detail, signal-to-noise ratio, and dynamic range under practical bandwidth, power, and quantum-efficiency limits.

papers.title: FlyingDrones: A Dataset and Benchmark for Optical Flow Estimation from UAV motion
papers.authors: Laurenz Ruzicka, Roman Pflugfelder, Daniel Cremers
papers.abstract_lede: Optical flow is an important cue for drone analysis in aerial surveillance, airspace monitoring, and long-range target tracking, where motion remains informative when appearance is weak.

papers.title: Self-Supervised Diffusion Models for Handwritten Signature Verification via Ruin Reconstruction
papers.authors: Peirong Zhang, Zhenhua Yang, Jiaxin Zhang, Moises Diaz, Miguel A. Ferrer, Umapada Pal, Wei Zhou, Lianwen Jin
papers.abstract_lede: Handwritten signature verification (HSV) is a critical biometric technique in legal and forensic authentication, whose efficacy hinges on the discriminability of signature representations.

papers.title: CMDiff: Left Atrial Scar Segmentation from 3D LGE MRI Using Conditional Mask Diffusion Model: A Feasibility Study
papers.authors: Jing Zhang, Bastien Bergere, Jonas Leite, Emilie Bollache, Mikaël Laredo, Alban Redheuil, Nadjia Kachenoura
papers.abstract_lede: Late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) cardiac MRI enables non-invasive assessment of left atrial (LA) scar, an imaging marker associated with atrial fibrillation ablation outcome. However, automatic scar segmentation is hindered by low contrast, the thin atrial wall, scarce labels, and extreme class imbalance.

papers.title: Masked diffusion as random sequential adsorption: an exactly solvable model for parallel decoding
papers.authors: Adrian Baule
papers.abstract_lede: Masked diffusion models generate text by reversing a stochastic masking process. Unlike autoregressive LLMs, which generate text one token at a time, they can reveal many tokens in parallel, at the price of an error, since tokens revealed together are drawn independently.

papers.title: StitchEdit: Stitching Depth Priors into Image Editors via Per-Layer Gradient Probing
papers.authors: Qin Guo, Dan Xu
papers.abstract_lede: Text-guided image editing with diffusion models struggles with spatial edits (e.g. manipulating objects, changing viewpoints, manipulating occlusions) that depend on the 3D structure understanding of a scene.

papers.title: Flux as a Codec: Zero-Shot Lossy Compression with Flux
papers.authors: Fuma Kimishima, Jinjia Zhou
papers.abstract_lede: We propose FluxC, a zero-shot codec that uses Flux as a compression prior. Although DiffC has shown that pretrained diffusion models can serve as zero-shot codecs, we ask how the choice of coding path and reconstruction method affects rate--distortion--perception behavior.

papers.title: IDPrior: Decoupling Identity Generation from Facial Image Synthesis
papers.authors: Fadi Boutros, Meriç Demirörs, Darian Tomašević, Vitomir Štruc, Naser Damer
papers.abstract_lede: Large-scale identity-labeled face datasets are essential for training modern face recognition models, yet collecting and annotating such data is costly and raises privacy and ethical concerns.

papers.title: FewStepRL: Fine-tuning Few-step Diffusion Models with Reinforcement Learning
papers.authors: Haitao Lin, Minsi Ren, Yang Li, Xingtong Ge, Zheyuan Hu, Peiyan Hu, Tailin Wu
papers.abstract_lede: Reinforcement learning (RL) has become a standard post-training method for diffusion models, but most RL objectives roll out the current policy at every iteration, and with a many-step sampler these rollouts typically dominate the cost of training.

papers.title: DiffSequence-Q: Diffusion Design with Quantum Assistance for Biologically Active Proteins
papers.authors: Ke-Xin Tang, Zhen-Qiang Weng, Kai Yan, Yao-Yao Lu, Yu-Ze Zhu, Hang Song, Jun-Jie He, Jie-Cheng Yang, Xiang Zhao, Lin Yang, Xian-Min Jin
papers.abstract_lede: Designing protein sequences that satisfy both secondary structure requirements and solubility targets remains challenging. We present DiffSequence-Q, a hybrid multinomial diffusion model conditioned on secondary structure at each residue and a continuous solubility target.

papers.title: Joint Electricity Price and Load Forecasting for Data Center Battery Dispatch Using Polynomial Diffusion Models
papers.authors: Matthew Van Ham, Yiping Liu, Xiaozhe Wang
papers.abstract_lede: The rapid growth of large-scale data centers (DCs) is increasing electricity demand, market volatility, and operating costs. Battery energy storage systems (BESSs) can mitigate these challenges by shifting electricity purchases from high-price to low-price periods.

papers.title: Learning Noise Optimization for Reward Alignment in Few-Step Generative Models
papers.authors: Hongeun Kim, Jeongsol Kim, Jong Chul Ye
papers.abstract_lede: Reward alignment for diffusion- and flow-based generative models is often formulated over stochastic trajectories, making it less suitable for few-step deterministic generators.

papers.title: Homology Features for X-Ray Hyperspectral Images Segmentation
papers.authors: Fethi Harkat, Guillaume Gey, Valérie Perrier, Kévin Polisano
papers.abstract_lede: Characterizing Multi-Energy X-ray Transmission (XRT) hyperspectral images presents significant challenges for traditional classification frameworks due to high-dimensional redundancy and non-linear spectral overlaps.

papers.title: Learning Pseudo-Riemannian Manifolds for Heterophilic Graphs via Graph Signature
papers.authors: Yun Young Choi, Asung Kil, Sun Woo Park, Minho Lee, Seokhwan Kim
papers.abstract_lede: Several widely used families of Graph Neural Networks carry a positive-definite geometric prior.

papers.title: Message-passing graph persistence
papers.authors: Jorge Luiz Franco, Arthur Queiroz Moura, Moacir Ponti, Amauri Souza
papers.abstract_lede: Message-passing graph neural networks (GNNs) are limited in expressive power by the one-dimensional Weisfeiler-Leman test.

papers.title: Graph Neural Networks for Resource Allocation in Integrated Sensing and Communication
papers.authors: Junyu Liao, Lili Chen, Tian Han, Jamie Evans
papers.abstract_lede: In vehicular integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) networks, each service-provider vehicle uses a limited power budget to serve multiple sensing targets and communication receivers.

papers.title: Spectral symmetry fingerprints in equivariant representations
papers.authors: Jiacheng Cen, Anyi Li, Ning Lin, Zihe Wang, Ji-Rong Wen, Wenbing Huang
papers.abstract_lede: Symmetry governs the organization of physical structures, while symmetry breaking reveals their transformations. In geometric deep learning, symmetry imposes rank constraints on equivariant representations, limiting the expressive capacity of equivariant graph neural networks (GNNs).

papers.title: Graph learning-assisted logic-based Benders decomposition for distributionally robust in-station train rescheduling under disruptions
papers.authors: Xiaobin Li, Yanbin Gao, Jianing Long, Wuming Lei
papers.abstract_lede: Uncertainty in resource reopening times complicates train holding and rerouting decisions when resource closures coincide with arrival delays and processing-time extensions.

papers.title: CasHyper: Modeling Multi-Factor Interactions and Asymmetric Influence in Cascade Prediction via Hypercomplex Algebra
papers.authors: Yansong Wang, Qisen Chai, Junjie Huang, Tao Jia
papers.abstract_lede: Cascade prediction aims to forecast the future evolution of information diffusion and is an important task in social network analysis.

papers.title: Towards Generalist Graph-Level Anomaly Detection
papers.authors: Junjun Pan, Yixin Liu, Yu Zheng, Fuyi Li, Alan Wee-Chung Liew, Shirui Pan
papers.abstract_lede: Graph-level anomaly detection (GLAD) aims to identify graphs that deviate significantly from the majority.

papers.title: Graph Symbolic Distillation: Decoding Graph Data into Interpretable Formulas across Materials and Chemistry
papers.authors: Yuxuan Yao, Harald Oberhofer, Karsten Reuter, Wenbin Xu
papers.abstract_lede: Graph data provide a natural representation of the interconnected structures and interactions underlying many chemical and materials systems.

papers.title: Spectral Convergence of Sparse Bipartite Graphs via the Line-Graphon
papers.authors: Roxanne Holden, Luana Ruiz
papers.abstract_lede: Pure point spectral convergence is generally unavailable for sparse graph sequences, where Laplacian eigenvalues may remain unstable under graph growth. This poses challenges for analyzing spectral operators underlying many graph-based learning methods, including graph neural networks.

papers.title: Wireless Link Scheduling with Graph Signal Diffusion
papers.authors: Teresa Shang, Romina Garcia Camargo, Yiğit Berkay Uslu, Alejandro Ribeiro
papers.abstract_lede: We solve long-horizon wireless link scheduling with per-link minimum transmission constraints. Fair distribution of resources across links and time steps requires stochastic scheduling, motivating a diffusion framework.

papers.title: Module-Aware Optimization for Graph Neural Networks
papers.authors: Guy Hadad, Haggai Roitman, Moshe Eliasof, Bracha Shapira
papers.abstract_lede: Different optimizers impose different geometries on parameter updates. Adaptive methods such as Adam and AdamW use coordinate-wise updates, while matrix-aware optimizers such as Muon utilize weight-matrix structure through orthogonalized updates.
